recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work on additional negation operators should be raised and resolved in a new Jira issue rather than treated as unfinished FHIR-13817 work.
issue_request: FHIR-13817 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core request to clarify how :not behaves for cardinality greater than one elements; the description proposed documenting the behavior and defining :excludes, while the final resolution specifically says to clarify that :not excludes a resource if any of the codings match.
initial_application: The issue was applied by svn revision 13379, represented in git by 331f9b3e724eda72d6e6f4b868d9b7fd51a4bb6b, which updated source/search.html to say :not returns resources that do not have a matching item and added a Composition.section:not example explaining that negation applies to the set, not each individual entry.
additional_context: The current search.html not modifier section and token examples still carry the set-level rule, and the Search Modifier Code code system defines not as resources that do not contain a match. A later 2022 modifier refactor preserved and expanded that behavior. Searches of Zulip and Confluence found only bot/commit references for FHIR-13817 and no substantive community discussion or later decision that changes the conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already satisfies the final Jira resolution, and adding a separate :excludes modifier would exceed the final disposition recorded for the issue.

evidence_items.learned: The final disposition establishes the set-level :not documentation target and does not preserve a requirement to define a separate :excludes modifier.

evidence_items.summary: The current not modifier section says :not returns resources with no matching value and gives a Composition.section:not example where negation applies to the set, not each entry.
